cleanIntro: The BANISH HD 762 INC is a 3D-printed Inconel .30-caliber suppressor built for hard use on gas-operated rifles. It is not designed to be fully disassembled, and its nine baffles do not come out: only the mount in the HUB rear thread can be removed. The service is a 24-hour soak, a brass brush in the blast chamber and a thorough clean of every thread, every 500 to 600 rounds. Everything about unloading your rifle comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Rifle unloaded, action open and visibly clear
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the rifle and open the action so you can see there is no ammunition in it. BANISH does not print a clearing procedure for your rifle. It sends you to that gun's own manual, a licensed dealer or the gun's maker if you are not sure how.
steps.prose: Both hands are about to be near the muzzle. An open action you have looked into is what makes that safe.
steps.quote: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.

steps.title: What it is rated for: 5.56 NATO through .300 RUM
steps.action: Check what the can has been fed. BANISH builds it as a 7.62 NATO/.308 Win suppressor, prints a cartridge range of 5.56 NATO to .300 RUM with no barrel length restriction, and recommends against solid lead or plated lead bullets.
steps.prose: Threads that fit do not make a cartridge suitable. If it has been fired with something outside that range, call BANISH before you fire it again.
steps.aside: Constructed entirely from 718 Inconel, the HD 762 INC has no barrel length restrictions and is rated for cartridges up to .300 RUM.
steps.quote: The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: The can may still be hot after firing, and a full-auto-rated can can be very hot indeed. Wait for it to cool, or use a suppressor cover or gloves, before you take hold of it.
steps.prose: Grabbing a hot can and twisting is how people get burned, and how a joint gets rushed.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use a suppressor cover (sold separately) or gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Hot after firing. Cover or gloves.

steps.title: Take the suppressor off the rifle
steps.action: With the rifle clear and the can cool, take the suppressor off. With the direct-thread mount it unscrews from the barrel threads; it was only hand tightened, so it should come loose by hand. On a quick-detach mount, follow the instructions of whoever made that mount.
steps.prose: BANISH prints how the can goes on and does not print a separate removal sequence. If it will not come off by hand, stop and call BANISH rather than put a tool on the tube.
steps.aside: Hand tighten suppressor only. Once snug, it is ready for use.
steps.quote: Before cleaning, ensure the firearm is unloaded and remove the suppressor.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: ⛔ Only the mount comes out — the baffles stay in
steps.action: The mount interface in the rear of the can is the one part an owner takes out, and it comes out later, after the soak. The can is 3D-printed, it is not designed to be fully disassembled, and the baffles cannot come out. There is nothing past the mount for you to open.
steps.prose: BANISH also says 3D-printed suppressors cannot be repaired. Anyone telling you to open it further is describing a different suppressor.
steps.quote: The additive-manufactured BANISH HD 762 INC is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface can be removed for cleaning.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

no.q: The additive-manufactured BANISH HD 762 INC is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface can be removed for cleaning.

steps.title: Twenty-four hour soak
steps.action: Put the whole can under cleaning solution, or plug the muzzle end and pour the solution inside, and leave it for 24 hours either way. Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or even dish soap all work. What does not is anything that strips the Cerakote.
steps.prose: The interval is every 500 to 600 rounds. Because the baffles never come out, the soak is what reaches them, so do not cut it short.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 500 - 600 rounds fired.
steps.quote: To clean, submerge the entire suppressor in cleaning solution. Or, seal the muzzle end of the suppressor and fill its interior with cleaning solution. In both cases, let the suppressor soak for 24 hours.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6
steps.warn: Be sure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote finish.

steps.title: Brass brush the blast chamber
steps.action: When the soak is done, scrub the blast chamber, the first chamber inside the mount end of the can, with a brass brush.
steps.prose: Brass is what BANISH names. The blast chamber is the only inside surface it has you brush, so leave the brush out of the baffles.
steps.quote: Once soaked, use a brass brush to clean the blast chamber.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Mounting adapter out, and every thread cleaned
steps.action: Take the mounting adapter out of the rear of the can and clean all of the threads: the suppressor's own, and the mount's inside and outside threads. Clear out any debris or buildup.
steps.prose: BANISH prints no tool or torque for the adapter; for a mount from another maker, use that maker's instructions. Carbon left in a thread is what stops the mount seating, and a mount that is not seated points the bore off line.
steps.aside: Always follow the manufacturer’s recommended installation instructions when installing any muzzle device, HUB mount, or adapter to your suppressor or firearm.
steps.quote: Remove the mounting adapter and thoroughly clean the threads, removing any debris or buildup. This includes the suppressor’s threads, as well as all internal and external mounting threads.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Let it dry, then the adapter back in
steps.action: Leave the can until it has dried, then put the mounting adapter back in before it goes on the rifle again.
steps.prose: At the next range session, 10 to 15 clearing rounds blow out whatever the soak loosened.
steps.aside: During the next range session, fire 10-15 “clearing” rounds through the suppressor.
steps.quote: Once clean, allow the suppressor to dry. Re-install mounting adapters and reattach to firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Protect the muzzle while the can is off
steps.action: Whenever the can is off the rifle for storage or transport, protect the barrel's threads and crown with a thread protector or other muzzle device.
steps.prose: A nicked muzzle thread is what starts a can crooked the next time it goes on.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH HD 762 INC PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's file name ends "-Final-10-26"; its upload path is /2026/11/). — WARNING, p.2

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the mount. On the CLEANING page (p.6) BANISH states: 'The additive-manufactured BANISH HD 762 INC is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface can be removed for cleaning.' It prints one cleaning procedure, and all of it (soak, brass brush, mounting adapter, threads) is in the routine lane above. This listing therefore has no deep clean.

cleaning.name: INTERIOR
tasks: Whole can submerged, or muzzle end sealed and the inside filled, for 24 hours
Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or dish soap
Blast chamber brushed with a brass brush after the soak
⛔ Never a solution that strips the Cerakote finish
⛔ Do not try to remove the baffles: they do not come out

cleaning.name: MOUNT & THREADS
tasks: Mount's inside and outside threads cleaned

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: Suppressor dry, mounting adapter back in
10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session
Thread protector or other muzzle device on the barrel while the can is off

reassembly: Can clean and dry, and the threads of the can and the adapter free of debris.
Mounting adapter back into the rear of the can. BANISH prints no torque for it: follow the instructions of whoever made the adapter for torque, thread preparation and alignment.
Rifle safe and unloaded before the can goes on. Barrel and suppressor threads clean and undamaged.
Crush washer: the book's words are 'If a crush washer is used with an existing muzzle brake, it must be removed prior to suppressor mounting.'

Direct thread: line the threaded end up with the barrel threads and screw the can on until it seats firmly against the shoulder. Do not cross-thread it: that damages both threads, puts the can out of line with the bore and can cause a baffle strike. Hand tighten only.
Quick detach: the muzzle brake has to be seated to the rifle's shoulder and timed with its shim kit. Then mount the can as the mount's maker says.
fncheck: With the rifle still unloaded: no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the suppressor mount, and nothing blocking the can. ⛔ If there is any gap, do not fire with the suppressor attached. Check that the can is still tight after the first 5 shots and every 30 after that, once it has cooled or with a cover, and fire 10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session. A 3D-printed can cannot be repaired: if it is damaged or defective, contact BANISH Customer Service before you ship it.
